title: 1960 AHSME Problem 32
statement: In this figure the center of the circle is \(O.\) \(\overline{AB}\perp\overline{BC},\) \(ADOE\) is a straight line, \(\overline{AP}=\overline{AD},\) and \(\overline{AB}\) has a length twice the radius. Then:

solutions.text:
Let the radius be \(r.\) Since \(AB\) is tangent at \(B,\) \[ AB^2=AD\cdot AE. \] Write \(AD=t.\) Because the secant passes through the center, \(AE=t+2r,\) while \(AB=2r.\) Hence \[ t(t+2r)=4r^2. \] Also \(AP=AD=t\) and \(PB=AB-AP=2r-t.\) The displayed equation rearranges to \[ t^2=2r(2r-t)=PB\cdot AB. \] Therefore \(AP^2=PB\cdot AB.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the radius be \(r\) and write \(AD\) in terms of \(AO\) and \(r\)
Use the tangent relation \(AB^2=AD\cdot AE\) together with \(AB=2r\)
